key_insight: R3MG-C builds a high-order multilevel preconditioner for continuous finite elements by clustering support points into agglomerates and enriching coarse spaces with locally embedded polynomial modes, improving robustness for high-order PDE discretizations.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical black-box preconditioning strategy for large finite element linear systems, especially when standard AMG becomes less effective on high-order meshes.
method: Recursively partitions finite-element support points with an R-tree using axis-aligned bounding boxes to form multilevel agglomerates.
Constructs prolongation and Galerkin coarse operators directly from point coordinates, without needing an explicit mesh hierarchy.
Uses continuous interpolation of local discontinuous polynomial coarse spaces of degree p'>0, extending the Nicolaides coarse space to higher order.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports two- and three-dimensional numerical experiments showing stable CG-V-cycle iteration counts and good performance in regimes where standard AMG deteriorates.
watch_item: The theoretical guarantees rely on assumptions such as uniform box regularity, interpolation stability, and stable decomposition, which may affect robustness in complex geometries or highly irregular agglomerations.
paper_title: R3MG-C: a high-order algebraic-geometric multilevel preconditioner for continuous finite element discretizations
